subject: Estimating prior hyperparameters for the Matern auto-correlation

messages.author: 642793e0109b8c57
messages.subject: Estimating prior hyperparameters for the Matern auto-correlation
parts:
Dear INLA experts,

I want to use a Matern autocorrelation function to model “intrinsic” autocorrelation in the distribution of fish eggs, i.e., the autocorrelation which cannot be explained with any external factor like temperature or water depth. Conceptually, my model of fish egg abundance would be the sum of a deterministic fixed part depending on environmental factors and a random effect explaining only intrinsic auto-correlation:

Response = GLM on environmental factors + random spatial effect    (1)

where the “random spatial effect” would arise from a Matern function with some range and variance (amplitude?). I know that I can let INLA to “freely” find optimal values for these Matern  (hyper)parameters. However, I have good reasons (details omitted for brevity) to give a *fixed* value for the range of the Matern function. I know that I can do this with:

spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(MeshA, prior.range = c(range0, Prange), prior.sigma = c(sigma0, Psigma))

where range0 is my estimate of the auto-correlation scale for intrinsic autocorrelation and Prange should be NA. Now these are my questions:

1) How can I get such prior (fixed) estimate for range0 which is consistent with my model (1)? Here is the one possibility I can think of:

1.a) Fit the “GLM on environmental factors” without random effect;

1.b) Estimate an empirical (isotropic) auto-correlation function rho(R) of the model residuals as function of distance R by defining distance classes between the observational points and using some simple estimator of auto-correlation;

1.c) Use the graphic of rho(R) to get an estimate of range0 (e.g., first zero-crossing of rho(R) or half decay from the maximum) or, if we want to get fancy, use non-linear methods to fit the parameters of the Matern function;

1.d) Once range0 is obtained, fit equation (1) with the prescribed Matern function with INLA.

Correct? Are there other options?

2) If I let INLA to freely fit the Matern parameters: how can I know and/or extract the resulting values after the fit (i.e., how to extract the values of the posterior Matern hyperparameters)?

messages.author: 642793e0109b8c57
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Estimating prior hyperparameters for the Matern auto-correlation
parts:
Thanks for the answer, Håvard!

I assume that your suggestion to read the book refers only (or mostly) to my point (1). I'll take a look to the book to find out how to give initial values for the hyperparameters for the prior of the Matern autocorrelation, I suppose that my suggested procedure with the GLM residuals is somehow wrong (or too simple).

Relating my point (2) (how to extract the values of the posterior Matern hyperparameters), I think that I found the answer in SPDEhowto.pdf of the vignettes (obtained by typing browseVignettes(package="INLA") in the R command line), i.e. what I was looking for was

MODS$summary.hyperpar

this gives all  hyperparamters, including those of the error (or residual) probability distributions (e.g., the power parameter of the Twedie distribution) and also those of the Matern function (e.g., range and variance).

All the best, Ismael.
